note: Re-judged 2026-10-27 (independent judge, after 2f36373081). RFC 4301 Section 4.4.1: "The ordering requirement arises because entries often will overlap due to the presence of (non-trivial) ranges as values for selectors. Thus, a user or administrator MUST be able to order the entries to express a desired access control policy." The STALE unit TestSpdUnstatedOrderTakesTheDefaultRank changed only by newRekeyedChild gaining its mode argument (child.Mode, the value the constructor previously copied from old.Mode); Mode does not reach childPairPolicy's priority, which still resolves child.PolicyPriority with zero mapped to PriorityChildSA, and newRekeyedChild still copies old.PolicyPriority. Assertions unchanged: operator rank reaches both directions and orders two overlapping 0.0.0.0/0 peers (positive; its revert record on childPolicies no longer verifies, producer-changed, and is owed a re-record by the author); unstated order is never 0 and takes the default rank (negative); an order capturing IKE is refused (engine and ipsec; the ipsec revert record on spd_policy.go validate verifies). All tagged units PASS at 95efd5421d. Observed this audit: disabling the zero-to-default branch in childPairPolicy turns TestSpdUnstatedOrderTakesTheDefaultRank red (rank 0 reached the SPD). The unit's rekey half runs on rank 0 and cannot catch a rekey that drops the operator's rank; dropping that copy in newRekeyedChild is caught by the untagged TestOrderedTransportChildRekeyAfterIKERekey, observed red this audit. Verdict stands.
